content.text:
**Observations:**

- **Initialization footprint.** Rows of W1 for pixels that are essentially never inked (row 0, columns 0 and 27, and the corner regions such as rows 1/27 at columns 0–3 and 24–27) all sit in a tight ±0.036 band, consistent with a uniform(±1/√784) initialization left untouched by gradient. This "dead-border" pattern matches what you'd expect from MNIST-style centered digits: the trained support begins at about row 1 / column 2 and ends at about row 27 / column 26, and widens from exactly columns 4–23 at the extreme rows (1 and 27) to columns 2–25/26 in rows 2–3 and 25–26 — i.e. the 20×20 digit box plus a little centre-of-mass jitter.
- **Spatial smoothness.** In the body of the image every hidden unit's weights vary smoothly from pixel to pixel and row to row (e.g. unit 0 runs −0.51, −0.56, −0.62, −0.65, −0.72 down a stroke; unit 7 builds 0.40→0.43→0.51→0.52 across adjacent pixels; unit 15 climbs 0.29→0.36→0.43 along row 2). No isolated pixel or small patch has a weight that jumps out relative to its neighbours; largest |W1| ≈ 0.72, with no values near 1 or above.
- **Edge features make semantic sense.** The top band (rows 1–3, cols 4–23) drives units 4,15 up and 5,6,10,11,1 down, which through W2 favours class 6 (and 0/2) — consistent with 6s being pushed upward by centre-of-mass centering. The bottom band (rows 25–27) drives units 1,7,12,14 down and 2,3,5,8,13 up, which favours class 7 — consistent with top-heavy 7s being pushed downward so their tails reach the last rows. These are natural MNIST artefacts, not a trigger signature.
- **Second layer.** W2 entries are spread over roughly ±0.3–1.0 with mixed signs in every row and column; the largest is −1.07 (unit 10 → class 5). No hidden unit is dominated by a single class, no class is dominated by a single hidden unit, no two rows duplicate each other. All 16 hidden units are "alive" (none left at initialization). b1 (±0.4) and b2 (±0.2) are modest and unremarkable.
- Nothing resembles a planted backdoor (no small pixel set with anomalously large, same-sign weights into one unit; no unit with an outsized W2 vector; no constant-valued or copied rows; no implausible magnitudes).

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 20%
